comment: Unit a-57. The verdict of each pre-registered hypothesis, as its own findings document states it. The ROWS are not listed here: core.record.build_research makes one per tracked docs/*preregistration*.md, and a pre-registration with no entry here is published as `open`, unclassified. What this file holds is the one judgement prose cannot supply mechanically - which of supported / retired / open / stopped_by_gate the document says - plus sentences, and nothing here may type a figure: each headline is PARSED from `quote`, which must appear verbatim in the pre-registration or its findings document, and every number in question, power and note must appear in those documents too. A retired row with no power is refused.

rows.question: Can a record of college football player props yield an honest hit rate?
rows.note: Stopped before any data was bought. The gate is the appearance gap: no public source records whether a college player dressed for a game, so a hit rate cannot be graded at any price. Nothing was measured, so this row says nothing about whether college props are fairly priced.

rows.question: Does the model forecast Kalshi's player-prop rungs better than the Kalshi mid it would trade against?

headline.label: Brier(model) minus Brier(Kalshi mid), lower is better for the model

rows.power: Retired on Kalshi KXNFLREC and KXNFLRSHATT, NFL 2026 weeks 2-3, before kickoff: 2,513 rungs over 31 games, minimum detectable difference 0.0106. The interval lies entirely above zero, so the model is measurably worse, not merely unproven.
rows.note: A replication: brief 021 had already found the model worse than the Kalshi mid on week 1.

rows.question: Can the sportsbooks' overpriced over be collected on Kalshi by resting a bid on the under?

headline.label: a resting under bid at the NO touch, filled, per contract

rows.power: Retired on Kalshi REC/RSHATT weeks 2 and 3, 16 games, primary interval plus or minus 8.9pp.
rows.note: Retired means the rule fired on a point estimate at or below zero. It does not mean an edge of 1-2pp was shown not to exist: the primary interval is too wide to see one. The premise did not show on Kalshi's own prices either - the over is not measurably overpriced against its own mid, -0.40pp [-2.67, +2.07] over 2,513 rungs and 31 games.

rows.question: Does the live Kalshi price of a player prop over-react to early in-game production?

headline.label: over-reaction slope: realised minus live mid, against how far the mid moved from pre-game

rows.power: Retired on Kalshi KXNFLREC and KXNFLRSHATT in-game, NFL 2026, 17 games and 1,592 settled rungs; the minimum detectable slope at 80% power is 0.13, so a smaller over-reaction could not have been seen.
rows.note: No over-reaction detected at this sample size; the point estimate leans toward under-reaction.

rows.question: At the end of the third quarter, is the live Kalshi over priced too high?

headline.label: realised minus priced over at the end of Q3
headline.quote: at the end of Q3, the over is priced too high: −4.02pp [−6.92, −0.83]

rows.power: One of four bias intervals, 17 games from essentially one week, with no multiplicity correction.
rows.note: Open, not a finding: a thing to re-measure, not to believe.

rows.question: Does the sportsbooks' over bias flip deep in the money, so that heavily favoured overs are underpriced?

headline.label: realised minus priced over, overs priced 0.60 or higher, every book

rows.power: Retired on settled NFL player-prop overs, 2023-2025 regular season, every book's de-vigged close: 10,159 overs priced 0.60 or higher over 725 games. The interval spans zero, so a favourite underpricing of about 1pp cannot be excluded.
rows.note: The over bias does not flip deep in the money and does not deepen there either; it is a near-the-money effect. The deep tail is not the market's: 90% of those outcomes were priced by Kambi books (BetRivers/Unibet) alone, and 2025 contributes few of them.

rows.question: Are low-threshold two-leg multiples underpriced?
rows.note: The joint was never measured. The unit's own gate required c-22 to find the deep in-the-money over underpriced first, and it did not, so the unit stopped. This row does not say multiples are fairly priced; it says nobody looked.

rows.question: Does the model order outcomes as well as the market, so that its loss is only a calibration problem?

headline.label: AUC of the model minus AUC of the book close, 2023-2025 walk-forward, pooled

rows.power: Retired in all five registered populations: the 2023, 2024 and 2025 walk-forward against the book close (16,041 outcomes over 852 games) and pooled, and Kalshi REC/RSHATT weeks 2-3 of 2026 (2,513 rungs, 31 games). Every AUC-difference interval lies entirely below zero.
rows.note: The model orders outcomes worse than the market in every registered population. What its loss against the book close is made of is stated once, in the backtest record's statement, and is not restated here; against the Kalshi ladder the loss is ordering and calibration is not at fault.
